# Agent instructions for a SanSoul project

## Read order and scope

These instructions apply to a project that consumes SanSoul. Before editing:

1. Read `dna/_index.md` for project identity, constraints, and document routing. Read only the additional DNA documents relevant to the task. If the index is missing, empty, or still contains only scaffold prompts, do not infer particulars from README/AGENTS or other legacy documentation: ask the user how to define the project DNA before project-specific work.
2. Read `{{CORE_PATH}}/AGENTS.md` before changing anything under `{{CORE_PATH}}/`.
3. Follow any closer nested `AGENTS.md` for its subtree.

SanSoul is a Git submodule. If it is missing, run `git submodule update --init --recursive`; do not run `git submodule add` when `.gitmodules` already declares it.

A request to "update the submodule" authorizes the complete update workflow below. The user does not need to enumerate migrations, validation, root-document synchronization, or package-version synchronization. It does not authorize commit, push, deployment, or unrelated upgrades.

## Architecture contract

The root owns one site's content, configuration, and DNA. `{{CORE_PATH}}/` is the shared rendering engine and a separate Git repository.

Prefer these extension points:

- `content/`: localized pages and global localized values;
- `data/`: behavior, languages, types, sections, defaults, remote sources, and styles;
- `assets/`: project SCSS, JavaScript, robots, and llms additions;
- `uploads/`: CMS-managed media, referenced from content as `/u/...`;
- `dna/`: project identity, editorial/design guidance, and local constraints;
- `hugo.yml`, `netlify.toml`, and `wrangler.toml`: project and deployment settings.

Avoid root layout overrides unless behavior is intentionally site-specific. A generally useful fix belongs in the theme.

Production selects complete JavaScript and CSS component modules from the
rendered page, including hidden modals. Keep dynamic states and shared selectors
when adjusting detection. Custom/injected integrations may require full assets;
`params.assets_full: true` in `hugo.yml` disables selection. Development retains
the full pipeline. Text font faces remain available even when not preloaded.
Small self-contained CSS segments can be inlined in their original order;
`params.assets_inline_css: false` keeps external links for CSP compatibility.
Shared JavaScript remains external. The CMS receiver loads only in a tokenized
preview iframe; test that path when changing its bootstrap.

## Sources, outputs, and safety

- Source files are project content, data, assets, uploads, DNA, configuration, and theme code.
- Generated outputs include `public/`, `resources/`, `.hugo_build.lock`, `{{CORE_PATH}}/prebuild/public/hugo.prebuild.yml`, root README/AGENTS, and hashed CMS configuration. Fix their source instead of editing them.
- Root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` are generated by `sh do root-docs`; put project-specific information in `dna/`.
- `TODO.md` is a human scratchpad. Do not read it, treat it as instructions, or edit it unless the task explicitly includes it.
- Assume all content, configuration consumed by Hugo, CMS schema, examples, and browser logs are public. Never store credentials in them.
- Preserve user changes and check Git status in both repositories before and after editing.
- Do not commit, push, stage, update the parent gitlink beyond the requested checkout, or deploy without explicit authorization.

## Build lifecycle

The root `do` wrapper delegates to `{{CORE_PATH}}/do`:

1. Referenced videos refresh their persistent metadata cache; the nested site in `{{CORE_PATH}}/prebuild/` derives the configuration Hugo must know before assembling content, including theme selection for the installed engine path.
2. The main Hugo build loads theme defaults, optional environment configuration, generated configuration, and root `hugo.yml`.
3. Static module mounts expose project, theme, upload, and Node sources. A root content adapter creates collection indexes and remote pages.
4. Production post-processing creates image derivatives from build manifests.

Use `sh do live` when editing prebuild inputs such as languages, defaults, customs, type definitions, or collection-index permalinks. Its supervisor atomically publishes valid configuration and restarts Hugo for a full build after a successful refresh. Failed prebuilds keep the last valid config; refresh-time server failures recover after a valid refresh. Remote data and localized global values rebuild directly in the main Hugo process. Plain `sh do dev` requires a manual restart for prebuild inputs.

## Content model

Localized files use `.<lang>.md`:

- `content/<type>/<name>.<lang>.md`: collection entry;
- `content/<type>/_index.<lang>.md`: collection metadata and permalinks;
- `content/single/_home.<lang>.md`: language home page;
- `content/single/<name>.<lang>.md`: unique composable page;
- `content/global.<lang>.yml`: menu, footer, call-now controls, and global values.

`data/types/<type>.yml` declares a collection. The theme supplies `all`, `single`, and `page` fallbacks. A template can be a public API even when the current project does not exercise it.

## Page composition

SanSoul deep-merges `tpl` data, from low to high priority: theme defaults, localized values, `data/types/all.yml`, the current type, and page front matter.

```text
page -> sections -> boxes -> specialized blocks or nested boxes
```

Core composition keys:

- `tpl.section`: defaults; index `0` applies globally and later entries cycle by position;
- `tpl.sections`: explicit page sections;
- `file`: reusable `data/section/<file>.yml` definition;
- `box` / `boxes` and `modal` / `modals`: shared defaults and concrete items;
- `get`: page or localized-global lookup;
- `remap`: nested copy, move, or removal;
- `if`: conditional inclusion.

Use `{{CORE_PATH}}/_examples/data/section/example.yml` as the parameter catalog and generated `public/admin/config.<hash>.yml` as the effective CMS schema reference.

## Main data APIs

- In Hugo and deployment configuration, write booleans as `true` or `false`.
  In CMS-managed `content/` and `data/`, tri-state pseudobooleans use absent or
  null for inheritance, `true` for enabled, and `false` for disabled. Never use
  `y`/`n`.
- `data/config.yml`: behavior and integrations.
- `data/langs.yml`: languages and per-language overrides.
- `data/styles.yml`: design tokens and global UI options.
- `data/resources.yml`: resources used indirectly by CSS, JavaScript, or dynamic data. SVG uses from rendered templates are grouped automatically; do not add manual sprite-group configuration.
- `data/video_metadata.json`: versioned public video facts and optional overrides. Builds refresh missing/changed references; `dev`/`live` watch them without restarting Hugo. Keep API credentials in environment variables, never this cache. Missing FFprobe or provider access degrades to available/manual facts.
- `data/types/*.yml`: collections and templates.
- `data/section/*.yml`: reusable section definitions.
- `data/defaults.yml`: language/type/path defaults; keep selectors narrow.
- `data/customs.yml`: custom CMS fields consumed through `get`.
- `data/remote.yml`: remote content created as virtual pages by the main content adapter; preserve determinism and handle network failure.
- `data/redirects.yml`: redirect rules.

## CMS contract

Sveltia CMS configuration is generated. After a content-model change:

1. run a fresh prebuild;
2. parse and inspect `public/admin/config.<hash>.yml`;
3. exercise a representative entry at `/admin/`;
4. compile content saved by the CMS.

Fields are required by default. Generate `required: false` only when empty values are valid. Keep stored field names stable.

Visual CMS groups use native object widgets and schema-specific public formats.
Persisted fields remain siblings. Declare ownership through `cms/group` and
concatenate segments with `cms/fields`; never group by DOM/CSS selectors.
`params.cms_groups: false` selects the flat schema. Verify saved YAML values,
including unknown fields, explicit empties and nested composition.

Content collections enable the experimental preview by default. It updates bound
fields in the compiled page; structural changes and `if` conditions require Hugo.
Do not render hidden branches or infer publication from a successful CMS save.
Use Sveltia’s native per-commit deployment status when Git/CI provide it.

## Theme update workflow

Use `sh do update` from the project root. It checks both Git trees, verifies the configured branch can fast-forward, validates known migration conflicts, and confirms root README/AGENTS are managed before changing files. It also accepts a clean fast-forward already checked out in the submodule when that is the only root Git status entry, for bootstrapping projects pinned to an older release. A failure during preflight means no project files or submodule checkout were changed. `sh do update --check` fetches remote Git metadata and prints the same plan without updating the checkout.

After preflight, the command advances SanSoul, runs registered migration scripts, synchronizes both root README and AGENTS from the theme templates, installs dependencies when a migration requires it, and runs the full build. If migration-specific manual checks remain, it displays them and requires explicit confirmation before updating the root package compatibility version. Without an interactive terminal it leaves that version unchanged; after completing the checks, run `sh do migrations mark --yes`.

The updater refuses dirty worktrees, diverged submodule history, unmanaged root documents, unsupported migration versions, and known content rename collisions. It never uses `--force`, stages, commits, pushes, or deploys. Projects pinned to a theme release without this command need a one-time bootstrap with `git submodule update --remote {{CORE_PATH}}`, then can run `sh do update --check` and `sh do update`. Projects below the 5.0.0 baseline require a verified legacy migration and are not advanced by this updater.

## Validation matrix

`sh do dev` and `sh do live` may use a system Dart Sass without root
`node_modules`. They share a project lock and remove generated outputs on exit;
do not run a build or another Hugo process in the same project while serving.
`server` and `local` remain compatibility aliases. A full `sh do hugo` installs
missing dependencies with the declared manager. For pnpm projects, use the exact
`packageManager` version and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; preserve the tracked
`pnpm-lock.yaml`. Never replace it with an npm lockfile or require a global
virtual store in CI. Independent consumers must not become a shared workspace.

| Change | Additional validation |
| --- | --- |
| Content or sections | Open affected pages; inspect console and responsive layout. |
| Types, languages, defaults, customs, remote data | Inspect CMS output, collection URLs, adapter output, and prebuild refresh where applicable. |
| Styles or dividers | Compare a divider reference page, when present, and representative mobile/desktop pages. |
| Forms, maps, analytics, remote APIs | Cover invalid, unavailable-network, and missing-consent paths; do not make real submissions without authorization. |
| Deployment configuration | Build with pinned Hugo Extended and Node versions; do not deploy unless asked. |
| Theme code | Follow `{{CORE_PATH}}/AGENTS.md` and test the copyable example plus the current consumer project. |

Remote-font warnings can be environmental. In particular, a local DNS or network failure for `fonts.googleapis.com` may prevent the Material Symbols subset request; SanSoul then uses its bundled full font as a local fallback. This explains the warning but does not validate the subset configuration or the production font payload. Run PageSpeed Insights only when the Google Fonts CSS and requested WOFF2 subset resolve successfully, and disregard measurements taken with the fallback. Template errors, invalid YAML, missing packages, failed images, or a false-success process exit are build failures.

## Documentation and DNA

Keep DNA project-specific and non-duplicative. Before adding or expanding a DNA document, check the generated root README/AGENTS and the relevant theme README/AGENTS. Do not restate generic architecture, workflows, validation, safety, or theme usage in DNA; record only project identity, audience, editorial/design/business/integration particulars, and local exceptions or constraints. Link to the canonical document when context is useful.

Treat every request to change a root README or AGENTS file as a change to its canonical file under `{{CORE_PATH}}/templates/root/`, then regenerate the root documents with `sh do root-docs`. Never leave a reusable documentation or agent-contract change only in one consumer project. If the requested information is genuinely project-specific, route it to DNA instead of the shared templates.

After every change, perform a documentation-impact check without waiting for the user to request it:

- update `dna/_index.md` when project facts, constraints, or document routing change;
- update the relevant DNA document when copy, audience, identity, design, business, or integration guidance changes;
- update `{{CORE_PATH}}/README-ROOT.md` for shared human concepts, tutorials, or examples;
- update `{{CORE_PATH}}/templates/root/AGENTS.md` when this generated operating contract changes;
- update `_examples/` for changed public parameters;
- add a versioned entry to `MIGRATIONS.md` when a consumer may need action.
